insights.title: Johnson & Johnson Just Raised Its Sales Outlook Again. Here's Why the Dividend King Is Still a Buy.
insights.claim: Johnson & Johnson raised its full-year sales and earnings guidance after beating Q3 estimates, but the stock fell 6% due to disappointing medical device sales. Despite near-term concerns about the MedTech division and a planned DePuy Synthes spinoff, the company's strong oncology business growth (16%+ in Q3) and reliable 64-year dividend streak make it an attractive long-term buy at current valuations.

insights.title: Johnson & Johnson: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors
insights.claim: Johnson & Johnson raised its full-year sales outlook after Q3 2026 operational revenue grew 6%, putting the company on track to exceed $100 billion in annual revenue for the first time. Strong pharmaceutical demand, particularly in cancer treatments, drove performance. However, the medical device segment faced headwinds with only 2.5% growth due to Middle East disruptions and China's bulk-buying program. Management plans to restore momentum through new product launches and is leaning toward spinning off its DePuy Synthes orthopedics subsidiary by mid-2027.
